heroText: Kigali is Rwanda's hilltop capital, widely regarded as one of Africa's cleanest and safest cities. First-time visitors should reflect at the Kigali Genocide Memorial, browse the murals and bars of Nyamirambo, and photograph the glass dome of the Kigali Convention Centre lit up at night. Kigali International Airport connects the city to gorilla-trekking bases in Volcanoes National Park, making Kigali a natural first and last stop on a Rwanda trip.

areas.name: Kiyovu
areas.text: Kiyovu is Kigali's central business hub, packed with hotels, banks and restaurants within easy walking distance of downtown offices.

areas.name: Kimihurura
areas.text: Kimihurura is an upscale hillside district of embassies, galleries and rooftop restaurants, popular with expats and longer-stay visitors.

areas.name: Nyamirambo
areas.text: Nyamirambo is Kigali's oldest and liveliest neighborhood, known for its mosque, cinema and colourful guided walking tours of local life.

areas.name: Kacyiru
areas.text: Kacyiru is a hillside government district near the Kigali Convention Centre, convenient for conference visitors and business travel.

airports.name: Kigali International Airport (KGL)
airports.text: Kigali International Airport sits east of the city centre, with taxis and hotel transfers readily available for the short ride into town.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Kigali International Airport (KGL) and central Kigali before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base in Kiyovu for an easy first Kigali stay near hotels, banks and the Genocide Memorial, or choose Kimihurura for upscale dining and embassy-district calm. Nyamirambo suits travelers wanting local culture and walking tours, while Kacyiru works well for conference visitors.
hotelIntro: Kigali hotel choice depends on purpose: Kiyovu suits first-time visitors wanting central hotels near the memorial and CBD, Kimihurura suits longer stays with upscale restaurants, and Kacyiru suits conference-goers close to the Kigali Convention Centre.
rentalCars: A rental car with driver is useful for reaching Volcanoes National Park or Lake Kivu, but Kigali's hilly city centre is easily covered by taxi or ride-hailing.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Kiyovu or Kimihurura for an easy first stay close to hotels, restaurants and the Kigali Genocide Memorial.

travelTips.title: Cleanliness rules
travelTips.text: Note that plastic bags are banned nationwide and littering is taken seriously, part of why Kigali stays remarkably clean.

travelTips.title: Airport transfers
travelTips.text: Arrange a hotel pickup at Kigali International Airport in advance, since it keeps arrivals simple after long connecting flights.

travelTips.title: Gorilla trekking
travelTips.text: Book Volcanoes National Park gorilla permits well ahead if combining Kigali with a trek, since daily permit numbers are strictly limited.

highlights.title: Kigali Genocide Memorial
highlights.text: Kigali Genocide Memorial is a clear heritage marker in Kigali, best used as a fixed point when grouping nearby streets, monuments and viewpoints.

highlights.title: Kimironko Market
highlights.text: Kimironko Market gives Kigali a concrete street-life stop, with food, everyday shopping and local movement that helps visitors read the city.

highlights.title: Inema Arts Center
highlights.text: Inema Arts Center gives Kigali a strong culture stop for museums, exhibitions or local collections, and works best as an indoor anchor in the day's route.

highlights.title: Kigali Convention Centre

highlights.title: Nyamirambo
highlights.text: Nyamirambo is a named stop in Kigali worth keeping on the route when it fits the day's transport, timing and neighborhood plan.

highlights.title: Mount Kigali
highlights.text: Mount Kigali adds outdoor time to a Kigali stay, with open space, views or waterfront breathing room between denser city sights.

nearbyIdeas.name: Volcanoes National Park
nearbyIdeas.label: Wildlife
nearbyIdeas.text: Volcanoes National Park is Rwanda's base for mountain gorilla trekking, roughly a two-and-a-half-hour drive northwest of Kigali.

nearbyIdeas.name: Lake Kivu
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Lake Kivu's lakeside towns of Gisenyi and Kibuye offer a relaxed contrast to Kigali, reached by a scenic drive west through the hills.

nearbyIdeas.name: Nyungwe Forest
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Nyungwe Forest National Park protects rainforest and chimpanzee troops in the southwest, a longer drive best combined with a multi-day itinerary.

history.label: 14th century
history.text: According to oral history, the Kingdom of Rwanda was founded in the 14th century on the shores of Lake Muhazi, around 40 kilometres (25 mi) east of modern Kigali.

history.label: 1300s
history.text: Alexis Kagame promoted an alternative theory that the city was established as a capital under Cyilima I Rugwe in either the 1300s or the 1500s.

Rwanda and neighbouring Burundi had been assigned to Germany by the Berlin Conference of 1884, forming part of German East Africa, and Germany established a presence in the country in 1897 with the formation.
The founding of Kigali is generally dated to 1907, when German administrator and explorer Richard Kandt was appointed as the first resident of Rwanda, and established the city as the headquarters.
Belgian forces took control of Rwanda and Burundi during World War I, with Kigali being captured by the Northern Brigade led by Colonel Philippe Molitor on 6 May 1916.

history.label: 1950s
history.text: Usumbura's population exceeded 50,000 during the 1950s and was the mandate's only European-style city, while Kigali's population remained at around 6,000 until independence in 1962. Post-independence era Kigali became the capital upon Rwandan independence.
In April 1994 President Habyarimana was assassinated when his plane was shot down near Kigali International Airport.
A masterplan, adopted by the city and the government in 2013 and supported by international finance and labour, seeks to establish Kigali as a decentralised modern city by 2040.

history.label: Today
history.text: Rwandan scholar Alexis Kagame, who did extensive research into the country's oral history and traditions, wrote that the name Kigali came into use after King Cyilima I Rugwe completed a conquest of the area.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The capital of the kingdom was at Nyanza, in the south of the country.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Kandt's house, located close to the central business district (CBD), was the first European-style house in the city, and remains in use today as the Kandt House Museum of Natural History.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Kigali's first businesses were established by Greek and Indian merchants, with assistance from Baganda and Swahili people.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Kigali remained relatively small through the remainder of the colonial era, as much of the administration took place in Ruanda-Urundi's capital Usumbura, now known as Bujumbura in Burundi.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Buildings that were heavily damaged during the fighting have been demolished, much of the city has been rebuilt, and modern office buildings and infrastructure now exist across the city.
